final_candidates.decision_summary: Corresponds to Spike Q498R, establishing direct electrostatic interactions with ACE2 Asp38 and Gln42 to drive one of the largest single-point affinity enhancements.
Corresponds to Spike N501Y, forming critical aromatic and cation-pi networks with ACE2 Tyr41 and Lys353 to consistently elevate ACE2 binding affinity.
Corresponds to Spike Y453F, enhancing hydrophobic packing against ACE2 His34 while maintaining structural integrity and protein stability.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 candidates represent the most reliable and high-affinity single substitutions identified from comprehensive DMS profiles, making further iteration unnecessary.

history.rationale: Equivalent to Spike N501Y, this substitution establishes favorable aromatic and pi-pi/cation-pi interactions with ACE2 residues Y41 and K353. It is a well-established affinity-enhancing mutation that significantly improves receptor binding.
N171Y (Spike N501Y) establishes critical pi-pi and cation-pi networks with ACE2 Tyr41 and Lys353, robustly enhancing ACE2 binding affinity across multiple lineages.

Equivalent to Spike Q498R, the basic arginine side chain forms new electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding contacts with ACE2 acidic residues such as D38. This substantially enhances binding affinity while preserving structural stability.
Q168R (Spike Q498R) introduces favorable electrostatic interactions with ACE2 Asp38 and Gln42, yielding one of the largest single-substitution affinity gains in DMS benchmarks.

Equivalent to Spike S477N, asparagine at this flexible loop position strengthens polar contacts with the N-terminal helix of ACE2 (near S19 and T27). Deep mutational scanning confirms it increases ACE2 affinity and expression.
S147N (Spike S477N) stabilizes the flexible receptor-binding motif loop contacting ACE2 and slightly improves both binding affinity and RBD expression.

Equivalent to Spike Y453F, the removal of the hydroxyl group improves hydrophobic packing against ACE2 H34 without destabilizing the core fold. It is experimentally documented to increase ACE2 binding affinity.
Y123F (Spike Y453F) optimizes hydrophobic packing at the ACE2 His34 contact interface without disrupting backbone conformation, consistently increasing ACE2 affinity.

Equivalent to Spike N439K, lysine introduces an additional salt bridge with ACE2 E329 at the receptor-binding motif periphery. This modification measurably tightens binding while maintaining RBD fold stability.
N109K (Spike N439K) forms an additional salt bridge with ACE2 Glu329, providing a well-established modest enhancement in binding affinity.

Equivalent to Spike Q493R, the arginine substitution can form favorable electrostatic interactions with ACE2 residue E35. It contributes to enhanced receptor engagement across multiple circulating variants.
In the unmutated Wuhan-Hu-1 background, Q163R (Q493R) introduces local electrostatic strain that does not reliably improve ACE2 affinity in isolation.

rejection.reason: In the unmutated Wuhan-Hu-1 background, Q163R (Q493R) introduces local electrostatic strain that does not reliably improve ACE2 affinity in isolation.

history.rationale: Alternative aromatic substitution at position 171 (Spike 501) that engages in hydrophobic and pi-stacking contacts with ACE2 Y41. It confers a confirmed boost in ACE2 affinity similar to N171Y.
N171F also enhances binding through aromatic interactions at position 171, but is functionally redundant and slightly less potent than N171Y.
Equivalent to Spike Q498H, histidine provides aromatic and hydrogen-bonding capability near ACE2 D38 and Y41. Experimental screens show improved ACE2 binding affinity relative to WT.
Q168H provides a moderate affinity improvement at position 168, though Q168R remains distinctly superior in interaction potential.

Equivalent to Spike T478K, the positively charged lysine enhances long-range electrostatic complementarity with the negatively charged ACE2 surface. It maintains fold stability and supports higher ACE2 engagement.
T148K (Spike T478K) contributes positive electrostatic complementarity near the ACE2 interface while preserving overall folding stability.
Alternative polar substitution at position 171 (Spike 501) known from mutational scanning to modestly increase ACE2 binding affinity through favorable local hydrogen bonding.
N171T is significantly inferior to aromatic substitutions (N171Y and N171F) at this position and does not warrant retention in the active pool.

rejection.reason: N171T is significantly inferior to aromatic substitutions (N171Y and N171F) at this position and does not warrant retention in the active pool.
